From: Linda Park <linda@aegis-analytics.com>

Cc: Aegis Analytics Legal <legal@aegis-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA appendix: local storage & erase timeline

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Aegis is very interested. Before we move to procurement, our legal team had a couple of focused questions on the DPA appendix you sent: specifically around where cached inference data may land (we're EU-first and require onshore control) and the exact mechanics and timelines for data erasure across live systems and backups.

Key Qs they flagged:
- Can you confirm that customer-generated prompts & short-term KV caches for inference are stored only in EU regions for an EU tenant?
- What is Redwood's erase window for ephemeral caches vs persistent logs? We need a clear SLA for onshore erasure (ideally <= 30 days) and scope for backups (do backups get wiped on the same cadence?).
- Are there any scenarios (debugging, incident response) where data could be transferred out of-region temporarily, and if so what controls/notice do you provide?

They attached redlines to the DPA and asked for a short call if we have any non-standard items. I've attached their redline v1 for reference.

Thanks — happy to sync tomorrow if it helps.

—Linda
Senior Procurement Manager
Aegis Analytics

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA appendix: local storage & erase timeline

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list.

Short answers up front:
- Yes, for EU tenants we actively provision inference capacity and KV/prefix caches in EU regions only; we do not route live inference data to non-EU regions for normal serving.
- Erase windows: ephemeral caches (per-request KV) are not persisted beyond session and are eligible for immediate deletion; persistent logs (audit/traces) default to 90 days but we can negotiate 30 days for your tier — we will need a DPA exhibit.
- Out-of-region access: in incident response we may temporarily route traces to a support cluster; that is rare and only under strict access controls — we can add explicit notice and an approval process in the appendix.

I've looped in Rishi (security/legal) for the redlines; he's added suggested language for the backup scope and a proposed onshore-wipe commitment. I've also attached a proposed appendix PDF that aligns with your ask (see redwood-proposed-appendix.pdf).

If that looks okay, can we get a 30-minute call tomorrow 10am BST to walk legal through the exact wording?

Cheers,
Naomi
Head of Sales — EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-appendix.pdf (pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Linda Park <linda@aegis-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on DPA appendix: local storage & erase timeline

Linda/Naomi — adding more detail on the redlines and operational guarantees.

1) Residency: we will commit in the appendix that for an EU tenant all inference inputs, inference outputs, and transient KV caches will be stored and processed in EU regions unless the customer explicitly opts into multi-region failover. This will be in Appendix A.

2) Erase commitments: proposed two-tier SLA:
   - Live data/ephemeral caches: deletion within 24 hours of customer request (or immediate on tenant termination) — these are in-memory/persistent caches with TTL controls.
   - Persistent logs & audit traces: default retention 90 days; offer an option to set 30 days for enterprise tenants with an associated pricing/commitment.

3) Backups: backups are stored encrypted and replicated within the same region; we propose a 90-day deletion policy for backups with an option to include a 30-day backup retention SLA in the SOW. Note: backups are immutable for a short replication window — physical deletion may require coordination (we will provide a certificate of destruction once completed).

4) Incident response/out-of-region: we will add an exception clause: temporary cross-region routing for incident response is permitted but requires prior written notice and a documented approval by the customer's security contact (or escalation to Redwood legal for emergencies). We will also log any such transfer and provide post-incident audit.

5) Controls: KMS integration + HSM support for EU keys; audit logs retained at customer-configurable granularity.

I'll draft redline language for these points and share. If Aegis needs 30-day hard SLAs for both live data and backups (not just an option), we should surface it as commercial — Marissa can advise on pricing impact.

—Rishi
VP, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dpa-suggestions.txt (text)

From: Linda Park <linda@aegis-analytics.com>

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA appendix: local storage & erase timeline

Thanks Rishi — that breakdown helps. A few clarifying points from legal:
- They want the backup deletion SLA to be identical to the live-data SLA (30 days) and not optional. They also require a certificate of destruction referencing the S3/object identifiers.
- For incident-response transfers, legal insist on a maximum 48-hour notification window and pre-approved escape clauses (e.g., court orders).
- They asked whether KMS keys for EU tenants can be customer-managed (BYOK) and whether HSM attestations are available for audits.

We're broadly happy with the proposed appendix if we can make the backup SLA non-optional and get BYOK for keys. If you can reflect that in the redline, I think we can proceed to procurement.

—Linda
